decisions.reason: The separate lemma lem-roots-of-unity-fft-complexity already states exactness and proves it in Proof 2.1: splitting even/odd indices gives both butterflies, and induction from M=1 proves the recursion computes the DFT. Proof 4.1 scopes initialization inside 'At a fixed depth', before the h loop, and discards that depth's arrays before advancing. Thus at degree h, t_k=(-(z_k-c_I))^h and w_{j,I}=a_j/(c_I-mu_j)^(h+1), so the accumulated polynomial is exactly Proof 3.1. Proofs 1.1-2.1 partition interactions with O(n log(2+M)) pairs; the geometric remainder and gate-error recurrence prove the stated certified scalar-operation bound. No power is carried between depths.

The title omitted the essential nonunitary LegT similarity, although the Statement and Proof 1.3 already state it correctly. Changed only the title to specify similarities. Entrywise, S0^-1 G^T S0 = -D^(1/2) S D^(1/2)/theta - D^(1/2) R D^(1/2)/theta, where S is skew-symmetric and R is the sum of two parity-indicator outer products. LegS and original LagT have the displayed rank-one corrections and normal scalar-shifted skew parts. The spectral theorem applies to these normal parts; the input/output transformations S^-1 B and S* C preserve the state model. N=1 and an empty parity column are harmless. Sources consulted: S4 Appendix C.1 and HiPPO Sections 2.3 and 3; the source LagT diagonal -1/2 differs from the original HiPPO diagonal -1, which the local proof correctly retains. Statement and proof unchanged; no interface propagation.

The unqualified HiPPO application in the Statement and Proof 1.1 conflates a fixed LegS coefficient matrix with the original time-dependent LegS dynamics. HiPPO Theorem 2 has coefficient G^S/t; already at N=1 its forced zero-state solution is x(t)=t^-1 integral_{t0}^t u(s) ds for x(t0)=0 and t0>0, which has no time-translation-invariant lag kernel. Repaired the application, F5 and Proof 1.1 to specify fixed G^S,G^T,G^L used as constant state matrices, with the same invertibility hypotheses, and explicitly distinguish the original LegS ODE. Preserved every general DPLR filter, accuracy and complexity claim. The resolvent reduction, (r+1)^2 block count, root permutation, M<2L, inverse-DFT norm <=1, e=r*delta perturbation and full-circuit rounding bound establish the remaining claims. No new prerequisite or choice principle is required.
